item.title: NACZ, Lotteries Board turn to skits to champion responsible gambling
item.description: Mbulelo Mpofu, THE country’s arts watchdog, the National Arts Council of Zimbabwe (NACZ), has partnered with the Lotteries and Gaming Board to harness the power of creative storytelling in promoting responsible gambling through the Responsible Gambling Skit Challenge. The initiative, which combines entertainment with public education, is calling on Zimbabwean skit makers to use their creativity and digital platforms to communicate the importance of making informed and responsible choices when engaging in gambling activities. Under the challenge, creatives are being invited to produce a one- to two-minute skit centred on responsible gambling and share it with the public through Facebook. Participants are required to post their skits on their Facebook pages, tag NACZ and the Lotteries and Gaming Board, and use the hashtag #ResponsibleGambling2026 to officially enter the competition. The campaign comes at a time when social media and short-form video content have become powerful tools for reaching large audiences, particularly young people. By involving skit makers, the organisers are seeking to move beyond conventional awareness campaigns and deliver the responsible gambling message in an entertaining, accessible and relatable manner. The competition’s top prize is US$1 000, with the winner determined by the skit that records the highest number of views and engagement. The deadline for submissions is 31 August, giving creatives several weeks to conceptualise, produce and publish their entries. Beyond the competition and its cash incentive, the initiative places emphasis on the need for members of the public to understand that gambling should remain a form of entertainment rather than become a source of financial dependence. Responsible gambling involves setting limits on the amount of money and time spent gambling and recognising when gambling begins to interfere with an individual’s financial stability, relationships, work or general wellbeing. It also means understanding that gambling outcomes are based on chance and that there is no guaranteed strategy for winning. The NACZ and Lotteries and Gaming Board are therefore using the creative sector as an avenue to make these messages more accessible to the wider public. For skit makers, the challenge also presents an opportunity to demonstrate how comedy, drama and storytelling can be used to address social issues without losing their entertainment value. A well-crafted one- or two-minute production can portray everyday situations, consequences of irresponsible gambling and practical ways of maintaining healthy boundaries. The campaign further highlights the growing role of Zimbabwe’s creative economy in public education. With digital content creators commanding significant audiences on social media, creative campaigns can potentially reach demographics that may not engage with traditional awareness initiatives. The organisers are encouraging participants to think creatively while ensuring that their productions clearly communicate the central message of responsible gambling. The competition also provides an avenue for emerging content creators to gain visibility, with audience engagement forming part of the criteria that will determine the winning entry. The challenge is expected to attract a wide range of comedic and dramatic interpretations of responsible gambling, while placing an important public-interest message at the heart of Zimbabwe’s increasingly influential digital creative space. At its core, the campaign seeks to remind the public that gambling should be approached with caution and self-control. It is not a means of securing guaranteed income, recovering financial losses or solving financial difficulties. The partnership between NACZ and the Lotteries and Gaming Board consequently represents an intersection between regulation, public awareness and the arts, demonstrating how creative expression can be deployed to encourage responsible behaviour and spark conversations around issues affecting communities. - Follow on X @MbuleloMpofu (via The Sunday News) #Zimbabwe #ZimbabweNews
